recipes.title: Scandinavian salmon potato cakes, light
recipes.summary: Tender salmon and potato cakes with dill, spring onions and a cool cucumber yogurt sauce. Extra cucumber and less potato and oil keep this high-protein snack light.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Prepare the potato, cucumber and spring onions in their listed forms.
Simmer the potato until completely tender when pierced with a knife.
Bake the salmon until opaque and easy to flake.
Mash the potato until mostly smooth while retaining a little texture.
Mix the potato, salmon, eggs, dill weed, spring onions and salt until evenly combined.
Shape the salmon mixture into small, compact cakes.
Heat the olive oil in a wide non-stick frying pan.
Cook the salmon cakes until golden and crisp on both sides.
Stir the greek yogurt, cucumber and lemon juice into a cool sauce.
Rest the salmon potato cakes briefly before serving them with the yogurt sauce.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the cooked cakes and yogurt sauce separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the cakes in a dry pan or oven. Freeze the cakes for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Scandinavian salmon potato cakes
recipes.summary: Golden Scandinavian-style salmon and potato cakes flavoured with dill and spring onions, served with a crisp cucumber and lemon yogurt sauce.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Prepare the potato, cucumber and spring onions in their listed forms.
Simmer the potato until completely tender when pierced with a knife.
Bake the salmon until opaque and easy to flake into large pieces.
Mash the potato until smooth with a few small pieces remaining.
Mix the potato, salmon, eggs, dill weed, spring onions and salt until evenly combined.
Shape the salmon mixture into evenly sized cakes.
Heat the olive oil in a wide non-stick frying pan.
Cook the salmon cakes until deeply golden on both sides.
Stir the greek yogurt, cucumber and lemon juice into a smooth sauce.
Rest the salmon potato cakes briefly before serving them with the yogurt sauce.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep the cakes and cucumber yogurt sauce separately refrigerated for up to 3 days. Reheat the cakes until hot and crisp. Freeze the cakes for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Scandinavian salmon potato cakes, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous batch of thick salmon and potato cakes with dill and spring onions. Extra salmon and potato make this a substantial high-protein Scandinavian snack.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Prepare the potato, cucumber and spring onions in their listed forms.
Simmer the potato until completely tender when pierced with a knife.
Bake the salmon until opaque and easy to flake throughout.
Mash the potato until smooth while retaining a little texture.
Mix the potato, salmon, eggs, dill weed, spring onions and salt until thoroughly combined.
Shape the salmon mixture into generous, compact cakes.
Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan.
Cook the salmon cakes in batches until deeply golden on both sides.
Stir the greek yogurt, cucumber and lemon juice into a creamy sauce.
Rest the salmon potato cakes briefly before serving them with the yogurt sauce.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the cakes and sauce separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the cakes in a hot oven or pan. Freeze cooked cakes for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Thai coconut rice porridge with banana, light
recipes.summary: Soft rice simmered with coconut milk, banana, ginger and cinnamon, then finished with toasted sesame seeds. Less rice and coconut milk keep this vegan Thai breakfast light.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Slice the banana and grate the ginger.
Simmer the white rice with the coconut milk and water until the grains become very soft.
Stir the banana, brown sugar, ginger, cinnamon and salt into the porridge.
Simmer the porridge until the banana softens and the liquid becomes creamy.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until fragrant.
Rest the coconut rice porridge until thickened slightly.
Serve the porridge with the sesame seeds scattered over the top.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat with extra water because the rice thickens while stored. Freezing is not recommended because the banana becomes watery.

recipes.title: Thai coconut rice porridge with banana
recipes.summary: A creamy vegan Thai-style breakfast porridge with soft rice, coconut milk, ripe banana, ginger, cinnamon and toasted sesame seeds.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Slice the banana and grate the ginger.
Simmer the white rice with the coconut milk and water until the grains are very tender.
Stir the banana, brown sugar, ginger, cinnamon and salt into the porridge.
Simmer the porridge until creamy and the banana is soft.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until lightly golden and fragrant.
Rest the coconut rice porridge until it reaches a spoonable consistency.
Serve the porridge with the sesame seeds scattered over the top.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and loosen with water during reheating. Heat gently until steaming. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Thai coconut rice porridge with banana, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous bowl of creamy coconut rice porridge with extra banana, rice and toasted sesame seeds. Ginger and cinnamon keep the hearty vegan breakfast aromatic.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Slice the banana and grate the ginger.
Simmer the white rice with the coconut milk and water until the larger amount of rice becomes very soft.
Stir the banana, brown sugar, ginger, cinnamon and salt into the porridge.
Simmer the porridge until thick, creamy and fragrant.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden.
Rest the coconut rice porridge until the texture becomes rich and spoonable.
Serve the porridge generously with the sesame seeds.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 3 days and reheat with additional water. Stir frequently during reheating. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Turkish zucchini fritters with yogurt, light
recipes.summary: Tender Turkish zucchini fritters with dill, spring onions and garlic, served with lemon yogurt. Extra zucchini and less flour and oil keep this Mediterranean lunch light.

steps.instruction: Grate the zucchini and prepare the dill weed, spring onions and garlic.
Mix the zucchini with the salt.
Rest the salted zucchini until it releases visible moisture.
Squeeze the zucchini firmly until as much liquid as possible is removed.
Mix the zucchini, eggs, wheat flour, dill weed, spring onions and garlic into a thick batter.
Shape the zucchini mixture into small, flat fritters.
Heat the olive oil in a wide non-stick frying pan.
Cook the zucchini fritters in batches until golden and set in the centre.
Stir the greek yogurt with the lemon juice.
Rest the Turkish zucchini fritters briefly before serving them with the yogurt.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the fritters and yogurt sauce separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the fritters in a dry pan or oven. Freeze the fritters for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Turkish zucchini fritters with yogurt
recipes.summary: Golden Turkish zucchini fritters flavoured with dill, spring onions and garlic, served with cool lemon yogurt. They make a fresh Mediterranean lunch for sharing.

steps.instruction: Grate the zucchini and prepare the dill weed, spring onions and garlic.
Mix the zucchini with the salt.
Rest the salted zucchini until it releases plenty of moisture.
Squeeze the zucchini firmly until it feels relatively dry.
Mix the zucchini, eggs, wheat flour, dill weed, spring onions and garlic into a thick batter.
Shape the zucchini mixture into evenly sized fritters.
Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the zucchini fritters in batches until deeply golden and cooked through.
Stir the greek yogurt with the lemon juice until smooth.
Rest the Turkish zucchini fritters briefly before serving them with the yogurt.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 3 days and store the yogurt separately. Reheat the fritters until crisp. Freeze cooked fritters for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Turkish zucchini fritters with yogurt, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous platter of thick Turkish zucchini fritters with extra eggs, flour and olive oil. Dill, spring onions and lemon yogurt keep the substantial lunch fresh.

steps.instruction: Grate the zucchini and prepare the dill weed, spring onions and garlic.
Mix the zucchini with the salt.
Rest the salted zucchini until it releases a large amount of moisture.
Squeeze the zucchini firmly until the shreds feel relatively dry.
Mix the zucchini, eggs, wheat flour, dill weed, spring onions and garlic into a thick batter.
Shape the zucchini mixture into generous, flat fritters.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the zucchini fritters in batches until deeply golden and firm in the centre.
Stir the greek yogurt with the lemon juice until creamy.
Rest the Turkish zucchini fritters briefly before serving them with the yogurt.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the fritters and yogurt sauce separately for up to 3 days. Reheat in an oven or frying pan. Freeze the fritters for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Vietnamese braised eggplant and tofu, light
recipes.summary: Tender eggplant and golden tofu braised with soy sauce, ginger, garlic and rice wine, served over a modest portion of rice. Extra eggplant keeps the vegetarian dinner light.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep it covered so the grains finish steaming.
Prepare the tofu, eggplant, garlic, ginger and spring onions in their listed forms.
Stir the vegetable broth, soy sauce, rice wine and brown sugar together.
Heat the sesame oil in a wide non-stick pan.
Brown the tofu until golden on several sides.
Cook the eggplant until softened and lightly coloured.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir until fragrant.
Pour in the broth mixture and braise until the eggplant is tender and the sauce coats the tofu.
Finish the braised eggplant and tofu with the spring onions.
Serve the Vietnamese braise with the white rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the braise and rice separately for up to 3 days. Reheat gently until steaming. Freeze the braise for up to 1 month, though the tofu will become firmer.

recipes.title: Vietnamese braised eggplant and tofu
recipes.summary: Golden tofu and silky eggplant braised in a savoury Vietnamese-style sauce with soy, rice wine, ginger and garlic, served with steamed rice.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep it covered so the grains finish steaming.
Prepare the tofu, eggplant, garlic, ginger and spring onions in their listed forms.
Stir the vegetable broth, soy sauce, rice wine and brown sugar together.
Heat the sesame oil in a wide non-stick pan.
Brown the tofu until crisp and golden on several sides.
Cook the eggplant until softened and browned at the edges.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir until fragrant.
Pour in the broth mixture and braise until the eggplant is silky and the sauce is glossy.
Finish the braised eggplant and tofu with the spring onions.
Serve the Vietnamese braise with the white rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and store the rice separately. Reheat over low heat until hot. Freeze the braised tofu and eggplant for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Vietnamese braised eggplant and tofu, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Vietnamese-style braise with extra golden tofu, silky eggplant and steamed rice. The soy, ginger and rice-wine sauce makes a substantial vegetarian dinner.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep the larger portion covered so it finishes steaming evenly.
Prepare the tofu, eggplant, garlic, ginger and spring onions in their listed forms.
Stir the vegetable broth, soy sauce, rice wine and brown sugar together.
Heat the sesame oil in a large non-stick pan.
Brown the tofu in batches until deeply golden.
Cook the eggplant until browned and beginning to collapse.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir until fragrant.
Pour in the broth mixture and braise until the eggplant is very tender and the sauce coats the tofu.
Finish the braised eggplant and tofu generously with the spring onions.
Serve the Vietnamese braise with the white rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 3 days and reheat gently with a splash of vegetable broth if needed. Freeze the braise for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Nigerian meat pies, light
recipes.summary: Baked Nigerian-style hand pies with a tender pastry and a savoury beef, potato, carrot and onion filling. More vegetables and less butter keep this version lighter.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Rub the wheat flour, butter and half the salt together until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Mix the whole milk, half the water and most of the eggs into the wheat flour mixture to form a soft dough.
Rest the dough in the refrigerator until firm enough to roll.
Prepare the ground beef, potato, carrot and onion in their listed forms.
Cook the ground beef until browned and no pink remains.
Add the potato, carrot, onion, tomato paste, paprika, thyme and remaining salt and cook until the onion softens.
Add the remaining water and simmer until the potato and carrot are tender and the filling is thick.
Cool the meat pie filling until it is no longer steaming.
Roll the dough into a thin, even sheet.
Fill and seal the dough into individual meat pies.
Brush the meat pies with the remaining eggs.
Bake the Nigerian meat pies until the pastry is golden and crisp.
Rest the meat pies before serving so the filling cools slightly.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat in a hot oven until the pastry is crisp. Freeze baked meat pies for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Nigerian meat pies
recipes.summary: Golden Nigerian-style meat pies filled with seasoned ground beef, potatoes, carrots and onion. The buttery pastry is crisp outside and tender within.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Rub the wheat flour, butter and half the salt together until coarse crumbs form.
Mix the whole milk, half the water and most of the eggs into the wheat flour mixture to form a soft dough.
Rest the dough in the refrigerator until firm and easy to handle.
Prepare the ground beef, potato, carrot and onion in their listed forms.
Cook the ground beef until browned and crumbly.
Add the potato, carrot, onion, tomato paste, paprika, thyme and remaining salt and cook until fragrant.
Add the remaining water and simmer until the vegetables are tender and the filling is thick.
Cool the meat pie filling until it reaches room temperature.
Roll the dough into a thin, even sheet.
Fill and seal the dough into individual meat pies.
Brush the meat pies with the remaining eggs.
Bake the Nigerian meat pies until deeply golden and crisp.
Rest the meat pies before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat in the oven for the best pastry texture. Freeze cooled meat pies for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Nigerian meat pies, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous batch of large Nigerian meat pies with extra beef and rich buttery pastry. The substantial hand pies have a deeply savoury potato and carrot filling.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Rub the wheat flour, butter and half the salt together until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Mix the whole milk, half the water and most of the eggs into the wheat flour mixture to form a rich dough.
Rest the dough in the refrigerator until completely firm.
Prepare the ground beef, potato, carrot and onion in their listed forms.
Cook the ground beef until deeply browned and crumbly.
Add the potato, carrot, onion, tomato paste, paprika, thyme and remaining salt and cook until fragrant.
Add the remaining water and simmer until the larger filling is tender and thick.
Cool the meat pie filling completely before assembling the pies.
Roll the dough into a large, even sheet.
Fill and seal the dough into generous individual meat pies.
Brush the meat pies with the remaining eggs.
Bake the Nigerian meat pies until deeply golden and crisp throughout.
Rest the meat pies before serving so the filling settles.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 3 days and reheat in a hot oven. Freeze the baked meat pies for up to 2 months and thaw before reheating.
